title: Kauravas
body:
Kauravas

Impressed by Gandhari's unwavering dedication to her husband, Sage Vyasa granted her a boon of having one hundred sons. She became pregnant, but her pregnancy continued for an unusually long period of two years. When she heard the news that Kunti had given birth to Yudhishthira, Gandhari was struck with frustration and beat her womb.
Upon hitting her womb, a cold, lifeless grey mass of tissue fell out. Stricken with horror, she implored Vyasa for assistance. Vyasa took the tissue, divided it into precisely one hundred parts, and placed them in one hundred earthen pots filled with ghee to incubate. At Gandhari's request for a daughter, he made an additional part and left it to incubate in an extra pot as well.
After two years of incubation, the first pot was opened. As soon as the firstborn was emptied, palace dogs started to howl, accompanied by roaring thunder and ominous portents. Bheeshma, Vidura, and Vyasa saw this as a catastrophic omen and pleaded with Dhritarashtra and Gandhari to eliminate the child to prevent the future destruction of their race. Gandhari refused, declaring she would not abandon her firstborn. This child was Duryodhana. The other pots were subsequently opened, birthing his ninety-nine brothers and their sister, Duhsala.
